Ben / Lauren —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Acme's requested edits. High-level recommendation: push for mutual exclusion language but accept a narrow, enumerated carve-out for: (i) fees, fines or penalties imposed by regulators arising from Redwood's breach of its data protection obligations; (ii) third-party claims against the customer arising from Redwood's negligent data handling; and (iii) out-of-pocket costs for immediate containment and remediation of a breach (limited to 12 months post-event and subject to invoices).

Rationale: A mutual exclusion preserves symmetry and helps prevent a precedent where Redwood is exposed to open-ended consequential claims. The narrow carve-outs are defensible because they relate directly to data protection obligations (which are core to our product) and can be capped/limited by time and invoicing.

Draft suggested redline (for Section 7):
"7. Limitation of Liability. Except as set forth below, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, indirect, punitive, or exemplary damages, including, without limitation, loss of profits, loss of business or business interruption. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following shall not be excluded: (a) liability arising from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) amounts payable under Section X (Payment), (c) regulatory fines or penalties directly caused by Redwood's breach of its obligations under the Data Protection Addendum, limited to the amount actually levied and subject to proof; (d) third-party claims for direct damages to the extent they result from Redwood's negligent or wrongful handling of Customer Data; and (e) reasonable, documented out-of-pocket remediation costs incurred by Customer within twelve (12) months following the event giving rise to the claim. Any liability under clauses (c)-(e) shall be subject to the overall cap set forth in this Agreement and shall not exceed the lesser of: (i) the amount of direct damages recoverable under this Agreement; or (ii) the insurance proceeds actually received by Redwood in respect of such claim."

Operational notes:
- Add requirement for Customer to mitigate and provide invoices for remediation costs; 12-month window is reasonable and aligns with typical insurance/timeliness limits.
- Keep the overall liability cap intact but allow carve-outs to be factored into the cap (avoid uncapped exposure).
- Consider adding a "foreseeability" qualifier in the definition of consequential to narrow "loss of business opportunity" language. Example: "consequential damages are limited to those not reasonably foreseeable at the time of contracting." But be careful — that could reintroduce ambiguity.

If you want, I can produce an inline redline of the full Section 7 and a short cover memo that calls out deal-level concessions (cap uplift, credit, or warranty length). I attached OLGA_Redline_Suggestion.txt with the inline text.

Recommend we propose the mutual text with the enumerated carve-outs and see if Acme will accept cap linkage rather than requiring one-way language. If Acme insists on one-way, ask for commercial quid pro quo (increased price, additional term commitments, or higher cap on our exposure).
